about: Rules this skill compares across US states and cities. Each cell names the page it was read from and how sure that reading is: 'official' was read on a government page, 'secondary' comes from recent law-firm or HR compilations that agree and cites the statute, 'lead' was reported but not confirmed. None of it is legal advice. Rules change; this file does not. Every cell carries the date it was checked, and the engine treats anything older than 180 days as due for a re-check.

minimum_wage.label: Minimum wage
minimum_wage.process_note: Rates cannot be merged: each site pays at least the highest of federal, state and local rates. Paying the highest rate everywhere is a business choice, not a compliance need.
minimum_wage.none_summary: No state rate above the federal $7.25.

overtime_daily.label: Daily overtime
overtime_daily.process_note: Payroll must compute daily overtime where a state has it; a weekly-only rule is not a safe national default.
overtime_daily.none_summary: Weekly overtime after 40 hours only (federal FLSA); no daily rule.

meal_breaks.label: Meal breaks (adults)
meal_breaks.process_note: Scheduling a 30-minute unpaid meal before the end of the 5th hour satisfies most state timings, but premiums for missed meals (California) and waivers differ by state.
meal_breaks.none_summary: No state meal break rule for adults in the DOL table.

rest_breaks.label: Paid rest breaks (adults)
rest_breaks.process_note: A paid 10-minute break per 4 hours worked meets every state that has a rule.
rest_breaks.none_summary: No state paid rest break rule for adults in the DOL table.

minors_work_permit.label: Minors: work permits
minors_work_permit.process_note: Each state has its own permit, issuer and age range. One national checklist can hold the rule 'no minor works without the permit their state requires', but the forms are state-specific. Hours limits are not covered here.
minors_work_permit.none_summary: No employment certificate required by the state (proof of age may still be required or requested).

new_hire_reporting.label: New hire reporting
new_hire_reporting.process_note: Reporting every hire within the shortest deadline among your states keeps one process.
new_hire_reporting.none_summary: Within 20 days of hire (federal outer limit).

e_verify.label: E-Verify
e_verify.process_note: Enrolling every site in E-Verify is lawful nationally, but a few states add their own procedures for employers who use it; confirm before switching on everywhere.
e_verify.none_summary: No E-Verify mandate for private employers (public employers or public contractors only, or none).

pay_transparency.label: Pay range disclosure
pay_transparency.process_note: A good-faith pay range plus a short benefits description in every posting, internal and external, satisfies every state posting law here. Some states add duties on promotions or on request.
pay_transparency.none_summary: No statewide pay range disclosure law.

salary_history.label: Salary history
salary_history.process_note: Never asking about pay history, anywhere, is the simplest compliant process; asking about pay expectations is allowed in every state that bans history questions.
salary_history.none_summary: No statewide ban on asking private-sector applicants about pay history.

fair_chance.label: Criminal history timing
fair_chance.process_note: Asking nothing about criminal history until after a conditional offer meets every timing rule. The notice and waiting steps before withdrawing an offer differ by state and city and need variants.
fair_chance.none_summary: No statewide fair chance or ban-the-box rule for private employers (federal FCRA and EEOC guidance still apply).

paid_sick_leave.label: Paid sick leave
paid_sick_leave.process_note: One national policy at 1 hour per 30 worked, with the largest annual cap among your states, covers accrual. Carryover, waiting periods, permitted reasons, notices and local ordinances still differ.
paid_sick_leave.none_summary: No statewide paid sick leave mandate for private employers.

predictive_scheduling.label: Predictive scheduling
predictive_scheduling.process_note: Fair workweek rules are local and industry-specific: notice periods, premiums, rest between shifts and offering hours to current staff differ by ordinance.

wage_notice.label: Wage notice at hire
wage_notice.process_note: One written pay notice at hire carrying every item any state asks for works in most states. New York, California and DC have their own forms or language rules, and some states need a signed acknowledgment.
wage_notice.none_summary: No state requirement to give a written pay notice at hire.

paid_family_leave.label: Paid family and medical leave
paid_family_leave.process_note: State insurance programs: payroll contributions, notices at hire and posters differ by state and change rates every year.
paid_family_leave.none_summary: No state paid family and medical leave insurance program.
